prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map lays out an indoor shop counter scene where a bright foreground counter surface and a right-side display case sit within 0.5 to 1.2 metres of the camera wearer, while a doorway on the left and a mirrored wall recess behind the counter extend 3 to 6 metres away. Behind the counter in front of the camera wearer stands a woman whose upper body is at an intermediate brightness corresponding to roughly 2 metres away in frames 1–3, decreasing to about 1.2 metres by frame 5 as the camera wearer approaches the counter and she reaches forward. To her left (about 0.5 to 1 metre from her) are a dark cash register and snack rack on the counter within her arm's reach, while the near edge of the counter, the register in frame 5, and the right-side display case come within arm's reach of the camera wearer; the counter occludes the woman's lower body below the waist throughout. Across the 5 frames, the woman turns from facing left and downward in frame 1 to facing and looking toward the camera wearer in frames 2–3, before looking down at the counter and extending her right arm forward in frame 5 as the left-side room exits the field of view. The depth map makes the continuous distance gradient along the counter and the planar boundary of the glass door behind the woman much clearer than RGB alone, though it is unreliable on the mirrored wall opening behind her (which appears uniformly black as an infinite void rather than a reflection) and blurs fine object boundaries like the wireframe snack rack.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against an unlabelled black background, consistently segmenting the woman behind the counter (`person`, ~2 metres away initially, closing to ~1.2 metres by frame 5) and intermittently detecting a second distant figure (`person`, ~4 to 5 metres away in the mirror/background to her left in frames 1, 4, and 5). Around the woman, the map segments several objects within 0.5 to 1.5 metres of her and 0.5 to 1.5 metres of the camera wearer, but misclassifies almost all of them: the chair backrest behind her right hip is labelled `cat` in frames 1 and 3 and `chair` in frame 4, the flat counter mat and counter surface in front of her are labelled `book` (frame 2) and `keyboard` (frame 5), and the glass pastry display case partially entering on the far right is labelled `tv` (frame 3) and `microwave` (frame 4). Across the 5 frames, the main `person` mask shifts from a left-leaning profile in frame 1 to an upright frontal silhouette facing the camera wearer in frames 2–3, and expands sharply in frame 5 as the camera wearer moves within arm's reach of the counter and she extends her right arm over the `keyboard`-labelled counter while her lower body remains occluded below the frame and counter edge. Compared to RGB alone, the segmentation map sharply delineates the woman's silhouette and highlights the small background person silhouette on the left, which is easily overlooked in the cluttered RGB image. However, the map is highly unreliable in semantic classification and temporal consistency, hallucinating labels (`cat`, `tv`, `microwave`, `book`, `keyboard`) and completely missing the cash register, snack rack, and structural walls.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders only a single yellow upper-body skeleton for the woman behind the counter (~2 metres in front of the camera wearer in frames 1–3, closing to ~1.2 metres in frame 5), leaving all scene architecture, counters, and background figures completely unrepresented on the black canvas. The skeleton's shoulder, neck, and facial keypoints show her torso and head angled downward and to the left in frame 1, rotating in frames 2 and 3 so her shoulders square up and her facial keypoints look directly toward the camera wearer, and then pitching downward toward the counter in frames 4 and 5. In frames 1, 4, and 5, her wrist and elbow keypoints extend downward and forward within her arm's reach of the counter surface (and within ~1 metre of the camera wearer by frame 5), whereas in frames 2 and 3 her right arm is omitted or tucked out of sight and her lower body below the hips is occluded by the counter in all frames. Across the sequence, the skeleton grows wider and shifts slightly right as the camera wearer approaches and turns toward her, culminating in frame 5 where both arms form a wide arch reaching onto the counter. This skeletal representation makes the exact 2D joint articulation of her shoulders, elbows, and head orientation far more explicit than in the motion-blurred RGB frames (especially frame 5), but it is unreliable in missing all magenta hand keypoints, dropping her right arm in frames 2–3, collapsing her torso width in frame 2, and failing to detect the distant background person.
